chunks: Abu Abdillah al-Bazawfari from Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Hasan from Muhammad ibn Ziyad from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who had two sister-slaves, and he had intercourse with one of them, then desired the other. He said: 'He should keep this one aside and have intercourse with the other.' I said: 'But his desire may be directed toward the first one.' He said: 'He should not approach her until he frees that one from his ownership.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a man who owns two sister-slaves and wants to have intercourse with both?
ai.summary: This ruling from al-Istibsar clarifies the distinction between the prohibition of simultaneous possession (jam') and the act of intercourse, permitting a man to engage with one sister while retaining ownership of the other. However, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) specifies that if his desire remains fixed on the first, he must emancipate her to break the bond of ownership, thereby removing the cause for the prohibition before approaching the second sister. This highlights the Shia juristic emphasis on the legal status of ownership as the primary factor in this specific prohibition.
